docs.title: Welcome to SENTINEL
docs.text: SENTINEL is an Autonomous Forensic Agent designed to triage digital evidence (EVTX, PCAP, Memory Dumps) automatically using Multi-Agent Large Language Models (LLMs) and deterministic Threat Intelligence engines (YARA/Sigma).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Agent Orchestration: Specialized Endpoint, Network, and Memory analyst agents powered by LangGraph.
  • Deep Artifact Parsing:
    • Endpoint: Parses EVTX logs and matches against Sigma rules.
    • Network: Extracts HTTP traffic, detects DNS Tunneling (via Shannon Entropy), and flags C2 Beacons (via statistical analysis).
    • Memory: Analyzes Volatility3 RAM dumps.
  • Threat Intelligence Integrations: Real-time enrichment against VirusTotal and AbuseIPDB.
  • Interactive UI: View a force-directed attack graph and chronological incident narrative in a beautiful Streamlit dashboard.
  • STIX 2.1 Export: Download industry-standard Threat Intelligence bundles.
  • 100% Local Processing: Runs entirely locally via Ollama, keeping sensitive evidence private.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Check out the User Guide to learn how to deploy SENTINEL using Docker Compose.

docs.title: SENTINEL Architecture
docs.text: SENTINEL utilizes a modular, multi-agent AI architecture built on LangGraph. By breaking the forensic analysis down into specialized sub-agents, SENTINEL avoids hallucinations, reduces prompt context limits, and allows for deeper analytical reasoning.

docs.title: High-Level Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Upload Artifacts] --> B(Parser Node)
    B -->|EVTX, PCAP, MEM| C{Supervisor Fan-Out}
    C --> D[Endpoint Analyst Agent]
    C --> E[Network Analyst Agent]
    C --> F[Memory Analyst Agent]

    D -->|YARA, Sigma, RAG| G[Lead SOC Analyst Agent]
    E -->|DNS Tunneling, C2| G
    F -->|Process Hollowing| G

    G -->|Chronological Timeline| H[Reporter Node]
    H --> I(STIX 2.1 Bundle)

docs.title: 1. 💻 Endpoint Agent
docs.text: Ingests raw Windows Event Logs (EVTX). It automatically correlates events against the internal Sigma rule engine and enriches matches with MITRE ATT&CK TTPs.

docs.title: 2. 🌐 Network Agent
docs.text: Analyzes PCAP traffic. Uses custom logic to flag anomalous DNS requests (calculating Shannon Entropy for DNS Tunneling) and tracks statistical temporal connections to flag C2 Beacons.

docs.title: 3. 🧠 Memory Agent
docs.text: Parses output from Volatility3 memory dumps, detecting malware strings and process injection techniques in RAM.

docs.title: 4. ⚡ Lead SOC Analyst
docs.text: Fuses the intelligence outputs of the specialized agents. Since each specialized agent summarizes its own domain concisely, the Lead SOC Analyst only processes the most important evidence to construct a unified chronological narrative.

docs.title: Persistent Case Memory
docs.text: All cases are tracked asynchronously in a local SQLite database (sentinel.db), providing persistent case management without external dependencies.

docs.title: Extending SENTINEL
docs.text: SENTINEL's parser architecture is designed to be highly modular. You can easily add support for new log types (e.g., Linux Syslog, AWS CloudTrail) or custom threat intelligence rules.

docs.title: Adding Custom YARA / Sigma Rules
docs.text:
To deploy custom deterministic detections, simply drop your rules into the respective folders:

  • YARA: Add .yar or .yara files to rules/yara/. The engine will auto-compile them on the next run.
  • Sigma: Add .yml or .yaml files to rules/sigma/.

docs.title: Writing a New Parser
docs.text:
To add a new parser (e.g., syslog_parser.py):

  1. Create a script in src/parsers/
  2. Define a function that accepts a file path and returns a list of ForensicArtifact objects. 
    from src.schema import ForensicArtifact
from datetime import datetime

def parse_syslog(file_path: str) -> list:
    artifacts = []
    # Your parsing logic here
    artifact = ForensicArtifact(
        timestamp=datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z",
        source_type="SYSLOG_SSH",
        host="ubuntu-server",
        user="root",
        details="Failed password for root from 192.168.1.5",
        ioc_detected="192.168.1.5"
    )
    artifacts.append(artifact)
    return artifacts
  3. Update src/agent/graph.py to route the new file extension to the appropriate analyst agent.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: SENTINEL can be run completely locally for maximum data privacy, or orchestrated via Docker Compose for production-grade REST API integrations.

docs.title: Running with Docker Compose (Recommended)
docs.text:
SENTINEL is containerized for seamless execution across operating systems.

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/udaygr0ver/SENTINEL.git
cd SENTINEL

# Start the stack
docker-compose up -d --build

This will launch: 1. SENTINEL API (FastAPI) at http://localhost:8000 2. SENTINEL Dashboard (Streamlit) at http://localhost:8501

(Make sure Ollama is running locally on port 11434 before starting the Docker stack!)

docs.title: Navigating the Dashboard
docs.text:
1. New Investigation: Upload evidence files (.evtx, .pcap, etc.). Select the Local LLM. Add optional API keys for Threat Intel. Click Start Analysis.
  2. Case History: Use the sidebar to toggle to historical cases. Click "View Report" to instantly load a past case from the SQLite database.
  3. Attack Graph: View an interactive node-link mapping of compromised hosts and IOCs.

docs.title: REST API (FastAPI)
docs.text:
For automation or SIEM integration, interact directly with the FastAPI backend:

# Start a new analysis
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/analyze" \
  -F "files=@evidence.pcap" \
  -F "llm_model=llama3.1"

# List past cases
curl "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/cases"
